quests.instruction: In which section of a grocery store would you find fresh apples and carrots?
quests.hint: Look for the section with piles of fresh plants.
quests.explanation: The produce section holds fresh fruit and vegetables. The bakery sells bread and frozen foods are kept cold.
quests.funFact: The word produce comes from a Latin word meaning to bring forth, like crops brought forth by farms.

quests.instruction: Where in the shop would you find milk, yogurt and cheese?
quests.hint: These foods all start as milk.
quests.explanation: The dairy section holds foods made from milk, and it is kept cold. Snacks and cans are kept elsewhere.
quests.funFact: Dairy foods are kept in fridges, so the dairy section is cold.

quests.instruction: Where in many grocery stores can you buy bread baked that same day?
quests.hint: You can often smell it from across the shop.
quests.explanation: The bakery bakes and sells bread and pastries. The seafood counter sells fish and produce sells fruit and vegetables.
quests.funFact: Many bakeries bake several times a day so the bread on the shelf stays fresh.

quests.instruction: Ice cream and frozen peas are kept in which part of the shop?
quests.hint: It is the coldest part of the shop.
quests.explanation: The freezer section keeps foods frozen. A bakery and a spice aisle are not cold.
quests.funFact: Freezer sections often have doors or lids to keep the cold in.

quests.instruction: Beans, soup and tomatoes sealed in tins are found in which part of the shop?
quests.hint: They sit on shelves and need no fridge.
quests.explanation: The canned goods aisle holds sealed tins. Dairy foods are chilled and produce is fresh.
quests.funFact: Tins are made of steel with a thin coating that keeps the metal from touching the food.

quests.instruction: At which counter could you ask for sliced ham or cheese to be cut just for you?
quests.hint: The worker slices it while you wait.
quests.explanation: A deli counter slices meat and cheese to order. Cereal and frozen foods come in packages.
quests.funFact: Deli is short for delicatessen, a word borrowed from German meaning delicacies.

quests.instruction: Why do many shoppers write a list before going to the shop?
options: To buy as many things as possible 🛒
To get through the doors faster 🚪
quests.hint: Ask yourself what is easy to forget.
quests.explanation: A list helps shoppers remember what they need. It is not meant to make them buy more or hurry.
quests.funFact: A list also helps shoppers avoid buying things that they already have at home.

quests.instruction: Which way of organizing a shopping list saves the most time?
options: Put them in order by color 🎨
Write them in a random order 🔀
quests.hint: Think about how the shop is laid out.
quests.explanation: Shops are arranged in sections, so a list in the same order means less walking back and forth.
quests.funFact: Shops are arranged in sections, and some shoppers plan their route through them.

quests.instruction: Which item is best to pick up last so that it stays cold on the way to the checkout?
quests.hint: It melts quickly.
quests.explanation: Ice cream melts if it stays out of the freezer, so it should be picked up last. Bananas and bread do not need cold.
quests.funFact: Some shops sell insulated bags to help frozen foods stay frozen on the trip home.

quests.instruction: How can you tell that an avocado is ripe and ready to eat?
quests.correctAnswer: It gives slightly when gently pressed 🥑
options: It feels as hard as a rock all over 🪨
It gives slightly when gently pressed 🥑
It looks very shiny and very wet 💦
quests.hint: Press it very gently with your palm.
quests.explanation: A ripe avocado gives a little under gentle pressure. A rock-hard one needs more days.
quests.funFact: Avocados ripen faster next to bananas, because bananas give off a gas that speeds up ripening.

quests.instruction: How can you tell that a watermelon may be ripe and juicy?
quests.correctAnswer: It feels heavy for its size 🍉
options: It feels heavy for its size 🍉
It has no color or smell at all ⚪
quests.hint: A lot of water makes it weighty.
quests.explanation: A juicy watermelon is full of water, so it feels heavy. A light one may be dry inside.
quests.funFact: A ripe watermelon often has a creamy yellow spot where it rested on the ground.

quests.instruction: Why is it a good idea to open an egg carton in the shop?
quests.correctAnswer: To make sure no eggs are cracked 🥚
options: To see what color the shells are 🎨
To sniff each shell one by one 👃
To make sure no eggs are cracked 🥚
quests.hint: Ask yourself how fragile a shell is.
quests.explanation: Cracked eggs can let germs in, so shoppers check the carton before buying.
quests.funFact: Cracked eggs can let germs in, which is why shops and shoppers check them.

quests.instruction: Flour is sold by weight. Which units measure weight?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what a kitchen scale shows.
quests.explanation: Weight is measured in kilograms and grams. Liters measure liquids and meters measure length.
quests.funFact: One kilogram is the same as one thousand grams.

quests.instruction: What does the checkout machine scan to find a product's price?
quests.hint: It is a pattern of black stripes.
quests.explanation: Barcodes tell the machine which product it is, and the shop's computer then gives the price.
quests.funFact: The first product ever scanned with a barcode in a shop was a pack of chewing gum, in 1974.

quests.instruction: A jar's safety seal looks already popped up when you pick it up. What should you do?
quests.hint: The seal should be flat before you open a jar.
quests.explanation: A popped-up seal means the jar may have been opened or may be spoiled, so a different jar is the safe choice.
quests.funFact: Many jars have a button that pops down when sealed, which shows that the food has stayed sealed.

quests.instruction: A food label lists ingredients in order. What does the first ingredient tell you?
quests.correctAnswer: There is more of it than the others 🥇
options: It is the costliest ingredient in it 💰
There is more of it than the others 🥇
It is the oldest ingredient in it 🕰️
quests.hint: Think about largest to smallest.
quests.explanation: Ingredients are listed from the largest amount to the smallest, so the first one is what the food has most of.
quests.funFact: The last ingredients on a list are used in the smallest amounts.

quests.instruction: A package says 'Keep frozen'. Where should it go when you get home?
quests.hint: The label gives a clue about temperature.
quests.explanation: Keep frozen means the food must stay in the freezer until you use it.
quests.funFact: Keeping frozen food frozen until cooking helps it stay tasty and safe.

quests.instruction: Which of these packages most likely says 'Keep refrigerated'?
quests.hint: It spoils quickly if it gets warm.
quests.explanation: Fresh yogurt must stay cold. Dry pasta and canned corn keep well on a shelf.
quests.funFact: Foods that must be chilled are usually displayed in the cold part of the shop.

quests.instruction: Which type of beans keeps the longest in a cupboard?
quests.hint: Germs cannot grow without water.
quests.explanation: Dried beans have lost their water, so they keep for a very long time. Fresh and cooked beans spoil quickly.
quests.funFact: Dried beans can be stored for a year or more if they are kept dry.

quests.instruction: A soup recipe calls for tomatoes, but fresh ones are hard to find this week. What could you use instead?
quests.hint: They are already cooked and sealed.
quests.explanation: Canned tomatoes are a handy swap in soup. Seeds would not make soup and apples are a different fruit.
quests.funFact: Canned tomatoes are often packed soon after picking, when the fruit is ripe.

quests.instruction: Which of these can be eaten straight from the package, with no cooking?
quests.hint: It is already cooked and packed in juice or syrup.
quests.explanation: Canned fruit is ready to eat. Dry pasta and dried lentils must be cooked.
quests.funFact: Canned fruit is usually packed in juice or syrup.

quests.instruction: A 500-gram bag of rice costs $2. A 1-kilogram bag costs $3. Which is the better value for money?
options: Both cost the same per kilogram 🍚
quests.hint: Work out the cost of one kilogram each way.
quests.explanation: Two 500-gram bags would cost $4 for a kilogram, so the 1-kilogram bag at $3 costs less.
quests.funFact: Shops often show a price per kilogram on the shelf label to make comparing easier.

quests.instruction: What is the best way to compare two similar cereals?
options: Pick the one with the brightest box 🎨
quests.hint: The facts are printed on the package.
quests.explanation: Labels show ingredients, sizes and dates, which are facts. Box color and height tell you nothing about the cereal.
quests.funFact: Labels let you compare ingredients, sizes and dates side by side.

quests.instruction: Why are fruits often cheaper when they are in season?
quests.correctAnswer: There is plenty and it travels less 🍓
options: The fruit is much smaller than usual 📏
There is plenty and it travels less 🍓
Shops throw the extra fruit away 🗑️
quests.hint: Ask yourself how much is being picked.
quests.explanation: In season there is a lot of fruit, and it often comes from nearby, so it costs less to bring to the shop.
quests.funFact: Strawberries are most plentiful in late spring and early summer in many countries.

quests.instruction: A family wants to cook spaghetti with tomato sauce. Which shopping list covers it?
quests.correctAnswer: Spaghetti, canned tomatoes, onion and basil 🍝
options: Bread, butter, sliced cheese, jam and cookies 🍪
Rice, honey, bananas, milk and rolled oats 🍯
Spaghetti, canned tomatoes, onion and basil 🍝
quests.hint: Ask yourself what goes into the sauce and what gets boiled.
quests.explanation: Spaghetti, tomatoes, onion and basil make a tomato pasta. The other lists would make different meals.
quests.funFact: Tomato sauce often starts with an onion softened in a pan.

quests.instruction: A list for omelets has eggs, cheese and peppers. Which item is still needed to cook them?
quests.hint: Something to stop them sticking to the pan.
quests.explanation: A little butter or oil in the pan keeps eggs from sticking. Ice cream and rice do not help.
quests.funFact: A little fat in the pan helps eggs slide out without sticking.

quests.instruction: Which choice makes the most varied vegetable shopping for the week?
quests.hint: Think about different colors.
quests.explanation: Choosing vegetables of many colors brings variety. One kind or none gives less.
quests.funFact: Buying vegetables of different colors helps bring a range of nutrients into the week.

quests.instruction: Which plan keeps food fresh and safe on a shopping trip?
quests.correctAnswer: Pick up cold foods last, chill them soon 🧊
options: Put raw chicken on top of the bread 🍗
Pick up cold foods last, chill them soon 🧊
Buy meat first and leave it in the car 🚗
quests.hint: Consider heat and about raw meat touching other foods.
quests.explanation: Cold foods are collected last and chilled soon, which keeps them safe. Raw meat should stay away from foods like bread.
quests.funFact: Raw meat is often bagged separately so that its juices cannot touch other foods.

quests.instruction: Which cart has the best mix of foods for the week?
quests.correctAnswer: Vegetables, fruit, rice, beans and milk 🛒
options: Vegetables, fruit, rice, beans and milk 🛒
Just bread, butter and plain crackers 🛒
Just cookies, chips and fizzy drinks 🛒
quests.hint: Count how many different food groups you can find.
quests.explanation: The first cart has vegetables, fruit, grains, protein foods and dairy. The others have very little variety.
quests.funFact: Planning a varied cart helps meals through the week feel different and interesting.

quests.instruction: Which shopper is using smart habits?
quests.correctAnswer: Makes a list and checks the dates 📝
options: Ignores dates and buys the biggest box 📦
Buys the first item on every shelf 🛒
Makes a list and checks the dates 📝
quests.hint: A little planning helps.
quests.explanation: A list and a date check help a shopper buy only what is needed and avoid spoiled food.
quests.funFact: A little planning before shopping can save time, money and food waste.
